papers.title_in_file: Robustness and Generalization in Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Lipschitz Regularization
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, sections 1 to 6 (method, setup, robustness, generalization, discussion); curriculum-learning details and references skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A quantum policy-gradient method with Lipschitz regularization (RegQPG) and a curriculum variant, tested on CartPole.

assertions.value: The authors report that training with the Lipschitz-regularized quantum policy gradient (RegQPG) improves the robustness of quantum policies on CartPole under additive Gaussian observation noise.
quotes: Overall, we can conclude, that Lipschitz regularization, as implemented in RegQPG, can significantly improve the robustness of quantum policies.
We show that training with RegQPG improves the robustness and generalization of the resulting policies.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical experiments on one environment (CartPole).
assertions.reader_inference: One benchmark environment; the PQC policy has few layers; no comparison with a classical policy network.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with the curriculum variant (CurrRegQPG), the fraction of runs that generalized over the widest tested range of initial pole angular velocities rose from 3% to 41% with regularization.
quotes: significantly increases from 3% to 41% in the presence of regularization
assertions.certainty_reason: Single environment, 100 runs per setting; empirical.
assertions.reader_inference: The 41% figure is for the regularization rate 0.1 column of Table 2; a rate of 0.2 gave a smaller gain.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments use the CartPole environment, with training performance averaged over 100 random seeds.
quotes: For experimentally validating the claims in this paper, we use the CartPole environment (Brockman et al., 2016)
Training performance is averaged over 100 random seeds.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental scope, Section 3.
assertions.reader_inference: The evidence is limited to one small control task.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Lipschitz bound may limit policy performance in certain scenarios and that less conservative conditions are future work.
quotes: Future work should consider less conservative conditions than those based on the Lipschitz bound in Equation (9).
it may limit the performance of QRL policies in certain scenarios.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of a limit, Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: Gradient Scalability and Taylor Surrogation of Quantum Cost Landscapes
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections II and III main text including Theorem 2 discussion, conclusion; appendices not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper on a Taylor surrogate for near-Clifford circuits and a Linear Clifford Encoder that keeps gradients from vanishing at initialization on small patches.

assertions.value: The paper proves that, for its Linear Clifford Encoder (LCE), the expected squared gradient norm at initialization has a constant lower bound independent of circuit depth, when parameters start on a sufficiently small patch near Clifford circuits.
quotes: in order to achieve a constant lower bound on the expected gradient square norm, independent of the circuit depth of
This is achieved by initializing the parameters on a sufficiently small patch
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 2 with Theorem 1, Section III.
assertions.reader_inference: The patch is classically simulable, so the result does not by itself give a quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Taylor surrogate matches Pauli path runtime guarantees with provable speedups on sufficiently small patches, and that a lower-bound analysis identifies a threshold where it shifts from polynomial to super-polynomial complexity.
quotes: We showed that the Taylor surrogate matches Pauli path runtime guarantees [21] with provable speedups on sufficiently small patches.
identifies the boundary where our Taylor surrogate shifts from polynomial to super-polynomial complexity, as established by our lower bound analysis
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 3 and 4 as summarized in the Conclusion; proofs in appendices not read by this reader.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not prove guarantees for the absence of barren plateaus beyond the threshold, and present the polynomial-decay regime strictly as a numerical indication and open hypothesis.
quotes: While we do not prove theoretical guarantees for the absence of barren plateaus beyond this threshold
We present this regime strictly as a numerical indication and an open hypothesis for future rigorous proof.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' statement of their own limit, Section I.

papers.title_in_file: Demonstrating Quantum Scaling Advantage in Approximate Optimization for Energy Coalition Formation with 100+ Agents
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results discussion of solution quality and runtime scaling, conclusion; supplemental algorithm reviews skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A benchmark of D-Wave quantum annealing, 1-round QAOA on IBM hardware and classical solvers on an energy coalition formation problem.

assertions.value: The authors report that D-Wave matches their best classical solvers on solution quality for up to 100 prosumers and reaches solutions within a 1% optimality gap from Gurobi for 150 prosumers.
quotes: D-Wave matches our best classical solvers (e.g., Gurobi and Tabu Search) for up to 100 prosumers (qubits) and achieves solutions within a 1% optimality gap from Gurobi for problems with 150 prosumers (150 logical qubits).
assertions.certainty_reason: One benchmark study on one problem family.
assertions.reader_inference: Authors include E.ON staff; the hardware vendor is not an author.

assertions.value: The authors report that D-Wave shows more favorable runtime scaling with problem size than the classical approximate solvers tested, yet remains slower than some classical methods such as QB-Solve at the sizes evaluated.
quotes: D-Wave exhibits more favorable time scaling with problem size than classical approximate solvers. However, for the system sizes we evaluated, it remains slower than some classical methods, such as QB-Solve.
The runtime of Gurobi, QB-solve, Tabu search, and simulated annealing scales cubically with varying prefactors
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical scaling fit from one study, Fig. 3(b).
assertions.reader_inference: The title says quantum scaling advantage; the body says the advantage is a potential one on preliminary evidence.

assertions.value: The authors describe their evidence as preliminary and a potential scaling advantage, and state that clear scaling is difficult to observe with up to 45 prosumers.
quotes: We provide preliminary empirical evidence suggesting a potential scaling advantage of DWave for a dense, real-world problem in approximate optimization.
DWave and QB-Solve demonstrate competitive runtimes, but clear scaling is difficult to observe with up to 45 prosumers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own qualification, Section I and results discussion.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning Advantages Beyond Hardness of Evaluation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, preliminaries, Section 6 discussion, theorem statements; appendix proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving identification-task learning separations for quantum functions under complexity-theoretic assumptions.

assertions.value: The paper proves that quantum functions are not random generatable unless BQP is in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy.
quotes: We show that quantum functions are not random generatable unless BQP is in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Contribution 1 in Section 1, proved in the appendix (Theorem 1 variant).

assertions.value: The paper proves that for a broad class of quantum identification tasks there exists an exponential quantum advantage unless BQP is in a low level of the polynomial hierarchy.
quotes: for a broad class of quantum identification tasks there exists an exponential quantum advantage unless BQP is in a low level of the polynomial hierarchy
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract and Corollary 1; conditional on complexity assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is conditional on a complexity-theoretic assumption and concerns constructed tasks, not typical ML workloads.

assertions.value: The authors state that the main-text results are presented under the heuristic form of the complexity-theoretic assumptions, since the analysis follows a distribution-specific scenario.
quotes: We note that the results in the main text are presented under the heuristic form of the complexity-theoretic assumptions, since our analysis follows a distribution-specific scenario.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' statement of scope, Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the manuscript presents exclusively theoretical results.
quotes: This manuscript presents exclusively theoretical results.
assertions.certainty_reason: Reproducibility statement.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks: Theory, Implementations, and Applications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, contents, Section VII (discussion, challenges, perspectives); body sections II to VI not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A review of hybrid quantum neural networks by Terra Quantum authors.

assertions.value: The review states that theory has established provable separations on specific constructed tasks, but that the case for a robust, scale-invariant advantage across typical learning workloads is not yet settled.
quotes: Theory has now established provable separations on specific constructed tasks, including some defined over large-scale classical data, yet the case for a robust, scale-invariant advantage across typical learning workloads is not yet settled.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review statement of the field; no single study.
assertions.reader_inference: Review authors are at Terra Quantum, which sells hybrid quantum ML products.

assertions.value: The review states that ansatzes that are provably trainable seem to admit classical simulation methods.
quotes: ansatzes that are provably trainable seem to admit classical simulation methods
assertions.certainty_reason: Review synthesis of cited work.

assertions.value: The review states that recent benchmarks caution that gains from hybrid quantum neural networks have not yet been demonstrated at scale.
quotes: While recent benchmarks caution that such gains have not yet been demonstrated at scale
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract of the review.

assertions.value: The review states that most HQNN results today are obtained by simulating the quantum layer classically, with on-hardware execution reserved for final validation.
quotes: Most HQNN results today are obtained by simulating the quantum layer classically, with on-hardware execution reserved for final validation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Review statement about the state of the field.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for Industrial Applications
papers.partial_detail: English abstract, chapter 3 summary and the statements of Lemma 3.1 and Theorems 3.2 and 3.3, Chapter 8 conclusion; remaining chapters and appendix proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: A PhD thesis (Sorbonne Universite, with Naval Group) on trainability, subspace-preserving circuits and dequantization of QML models.

assertions.value: The thesis states that barren plateaus can be avoided for subspace-invariant circuits built from RBS or FBS gates, provided the circuit is used in a fixed Hamming-weight subspace and under certain assumptions on qubit connectivity.
quotes: BPs can indeed be avoided for subspace-invariant quantum circuits based on RBS or FBS gates
provided the circuit is employed only in a given HW k subspace with fixed k and under certain assumptions on the qubit connectivity
assertions.certainty_reason: Lemma 3.1 and Theorems 3.2 and 3.3, Chapter 3 (proofs in Appendix A, not read).

assertions.value: The thesis states that when QML algorithms avoid the barren plateau problem, this is often achieved by reducing algorithmic complexity to the point where efficient classical simulation becomes possible.
quotes: when QML algorithms avoid key issues such as the barren plateau problem (a vanishing-gradient phenomenon that prevents learning), this is often achieved by reducing algorithmic complexity to the point where efficient classical simulation becomes possible
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion summarizing recent research.

assertions.value: The thesis states that designing quantum models provably resistant to dequantization remains a non-trivial task, especially when also avoiding exponential concentration of the loss landscape.
quotes: designing quantum models that are provably resistant to dequantization remains a non-trivial task, all the more so when simultaneously avoiding exponential concentration of the loss landscape
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's statement of an open limit, Chapter 8.

assertions.value: The thesis cites recent benchmarking studies as showing that many widely used quantum models fail to outperform well-tuned classical baselines.
quotes: Recent benchmarking studies [74] have shown that many widely used quantum models fail to outperform well-tuned classical baselines
assertions.certainty_reason: Cited result in the conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: Ground or Excited State: a State-Specific Variational Quantum Eigensolver for Them All
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, computational details, Be insertion results description, conclusion; derivation details of Section II skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A VQE variant (ss-VQE) that targets symmetry-adapted ground and excited states one at a time, tested by simulation on a small molecular system.

assertions.value: The authors claim that their state-specific VQE needs no prior knowledge of the ground state and can selectively target any low-lying excited state of a given symmetry.
quotes: Unlike all other methods, ss-VQE does not require any prior knowledge of the ground state and it can selectively target any low-lying excited state
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim of advantage over other methods.

assertions.value: The authors report simulating ground and excited states along the insertion pathway of a beryllium atom into a hydrogen molecule in the STO-3G basis, with ss-VQE results shown as dots against FCI values as lines.
quotes: We simulated the ground and a number of excited states along the insertion pathway in STO-3G basis where the core 1s orbital of Be is kept frozen.
The Solid lines are the FCI values whereas the dots are the results obtained from state-specific VQE (ss-VQE)
assertions.certainty_reason: One molecular test case; numerical agreement is in the figure, not stated in the quotes.
assertions.reader_inference: Agreement with FCI is shown in a figure; this reader did not extract numbers.

assertions.value: The authors state that all calculations used a statevector simulator assuming an ideal quantum environment.
quotes: we have chosen the statevector-simulator assuming an ideal quantum environment
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of computational setup.
assertions.reader_inference: No noisy or hardware run supports the near-term-device claim.

papers.title_in_file: Evaluating the performance of quantum processing units at large width and depth
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, benchmarking background, Section IV discussion and conclusions; detailed results sections not read
papers.what_it_is: A cross-vendor benchmark of 24 quantum processors using a linear ramp QAOA protocol.

assertions.value: The authors state that they applied the linear ramp QAOA benchmark to 24 quantum processors from six vendors, with problems up to 156 qubits and 10,000 layers.
quotes: We apply this protocol to 24 quantum processors from six vendors, testing problems with up to 156 qubits and 10,000 layers across 1D-chains, native layouts, and fully connected topologies.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' statement of their experimental scope, abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report that Quantinuum H2-1 was the only platform to pass the 56-qubit fully connected benchmark, and that the error-per-layered-gate metric does not consistently predict algorithmic performance, especially at scale.
quotes: (ii) Quantinuum's H2-1 is the only platform to successfully pass the 56-qubit FC benchmark.
(iii) The error-perlayered-gate (EPLG) metric does not consistently predict algorithmic performance, especially at scale.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results from one benchmark study at one time.
assertions.reader_inference: Results depend on hardware access at the time and on the single LR-QAOA protocol.

assertions.value: The authors report that the protocol remained stable over time, with less than 1% variation over two months.
quotes: remains stable over time, with less than 1% variation over two months.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical stability check reported in the conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the benchmark is designed to capture the raw performance of a QPU, and that changing the initial state, for example by warm-start initialization, introduces bias and invalidates statistical comparisons.
quotes: In general, these benchmarks are designed to capture the raw performance of a QPU.
Changing the initial state, for example via warm-start initialization [41], introduces bias and invalidates statistical comparisons.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of benchmark scope.
